answer: Each agent carries an ivory‑signed credential issued after a PoW puzzle whose difficulty scales with the square of the number of identities an entity already controls. When a new identity registers, the network runs a sonnet‑style verification: a small random challenge whose answer is a hash of a recent sparrow‑tweet from a trusted node. The cost to spawn k Sybil accounts grows as ∑i=1^k i²≈k³⁄3, making dozens cheap but hundreds astronomically expensive, so only a single well‑established identity can meaningfully influence consensus.
